home.title: FOUND: Foundation Data for Industrial Tech Transfer
home.tagline: Bridging Academic Progress and Practical Impact through Domain-Grounded Data
home.subtitle: ECCV 2026 Workshop

overview.mission: Foundation models have pushed computer vision forward, but their reliability often drops in real-world, domain-specific deployments due to long-tail distributions, domain shift, and operational constraints (privacy, safety, cost). Closing this "last-mile" gap requires not only better models, but domain-tailored datasets that capture rare yet critical corner cases and realistic variability. Building on the first FOUND workshop, we refer to this missing piece as Foundation Data: fine-grained, domain-grounded data designed to bridge academic progress and practical impact.
keyTopics: Foundation Data creation: collection from non-Internet domains, curation and labeling at scale, self-/semi-/weak supervision, and synthetic/simulation data
Practical tech transfer: adaptation, robustness to OOD/long-tail conditions, and deployment/evaluation protocols aligned with operating reality
Physical AI and World Models: data and transfer strategies for embodied, interactive settings
Temporal and multimodal streams, sim-to-real transfer, and safety-aware evaluation
Continual adaptation and domain-specific deployment protocols

callForPapers.title: Call for Papers
callForPapers.subtitle: Submit your research to the FOUND Workshop

core: Foundation Data creation: collection, curation, and labeling for non-Internet and domain-specific settings
Self-supervised, semi-supervised, and weakly-supervised learning for domain-grounded data
Synthetic and simulation data for bridging domain gaps and covering rare corner cases
Robustness under domain shift, OOD conditions, and long-tail distributions in industrial deployments
Physical AI and World Models: data and transfer strategies for embodied and interactive systems
Deployment-aligned evaluation protocols and responsible data governance for real-world AI

submissionGuidelines: Submissions must be handled electronically via the OpenReview submission website
Papers up to 8 pages for publication in the Springer proceedings, excluding references
paperFormat.reviewProcess: All submissions will undergo a double-blind peer review process. The review process will involve over 100 reviewers from previous FOUND workshops and the LIMIT.Lab/xpaper.challenge community.
paperFormat.publication: Accepted papers will be published in the Springer proceedings and presented at the workshop.

submission.description: The OpenReview submission website will be available soon. Please check back for updates.

callForPapers.bestPaperAwards: We will present Best Paper and Best Student Paper awards to recognize outstanding contributions. Award winners will receive certificates and will be highlighted during the workshop.

faq.question: Can I submit a paper that is under review elsewhere?
faq.answer: No, submissions must be original and not under review at any other conference, workshop, or journal during the review period.

faq.question: What is the page limit for submissions?
faq.answer: Papers up to 8 pages, excluding references, for publication in the Springer proceedings.

faq.question: Is the review process double-blind?
faq.answer: Yes, all submissions must be anonymized for double-blind review.

faq.question: Do I need to attend the workshop if my paper is accepted?
faq.answer: Yes, at least one author of each accepted paper must register for and attend the workshop to present the work.
